hard_rule: Any FAIL on an applicable invariant blocks RB1.

audit.rationale: RB1 is a qualified subset of the single SWAP5 kernel. No restricted second kernel is introduced.
RB1 kernel contracts remain independent of legacy files, formats, file units and paths. Release evidence does not move legacy I/O into the kernel.
Immutable parameters, committed dynamic state, forcing, numerical configuration and results remain explicit separate categories in the admitted kernel/runtime contracts.
Persistent restart state is committed physical/process state only. Solver scratch, worker state, Newton/Jacobian data and warm-start scratch are excluded from restart records.
Restricted parallel V1 and root-active parallel execution allocate heavy backend/transaction/runtime scratch per worker rather than per logical column.

Logical columns are scheduled through restricted serialized/parallel runtimes with pooled worker resources. RB1 does not impose one heavyweight solver instance per column or prohibit later SoA/pool/batch layouts.
Checkpoint, trial/retry, exactly-once commit or rollback semantics are required. Rejected trials cannot mutate committed physical state or the authoritative mass ledger.
Re-execution begins from the correct committed physical state. Numerical trial trajectories are not elevated to committed state and restart intentionally reconstructs scratch.
Kernel execution remains over generic [t0,t1]. RB1 adds no midnight, day, month or year assumption.
Direct MODFLOW predictor-corrector coupling windows are outside the RB1 release claim. RB1 must preserve the generic coupling seam and does not narrow it to daily windows.

Coupling contracts remain architectural kernel/runtime concerns even though broad coupled application release is excluded. RB1 introduces no design that prevents checkpoint, rollback, interface residual or conservative coupling support.
The direct operational H_SWAP=H_MF and q_SWAP=-q_MF contract is not exercised as an RB1 release capability. No contrary interface semantics are introduced.
Water mass conservation is a hard non-configurable release gate for every admitted physical RB1 path, including transaction, restart and MultiSWAP composition.
MODFLOW interface response tangents are not an RB1 release capability. The alternate/coupling interfaces remain open and RB1 makes no production sensitivity claim.
Broad coupled predictor/corrector production cost is outside RB1. No 6-to-9-run production coupling path is introduced by this release subset.
Serialized and restricted parallel real-physics MultiSWAP are REQUIRED RB1 capabilities. Worker-owned scratch and deterministic collection are release gates.
RB1 kernel/runtime contracts contain no compulsory one-to-one MODFLOW-cell mapping. Surface-fraction/tile composition remains a runtime/coupler responsibility.
Deep-vadose transfer is an optional external component and is not part of RB1. RB1 does not reinterpret bottom flux as deep recharge where such a transfer zone would be required.
RB1 does not release a deep-vadose/direct-coupling transition workflow. No stored-water transfer claim is made.
Full Richards is the sole RB1 production soil-water solver but remains behind the common soil-water seam. Ross/reduced alternatives are excluded without removing or hard-coding away that seam.
RB1 reuses the admitted SWAP5 process/runtime architecture and does not create duplicate restricted physics implementations solely for release.
RB1 process contracts consume hydraulic information through the admitted interfaces/views and do not require new dependencies on HeadCalc internal arrays or private numerical implementation.

RB1 admits REFERENCE numerical policy only unless a separately qualified path is explicit. Performance evidence does not silently change physical processes, parameters, conservation or boundary semantics.

Unsupported profiles fail closed and restricted execution cost is diagnosed. F-PE03 negative tail evidence is retained. RB1 makes no invented p95/p99 or bounded-cost SLA and therefore does not hide unresolved tail research.
Full-accuracy Full Richards REFERENCE mode is the RB1 reference and remains available.
RB1 requires per-column/interval status, accepted/rejected/retry and available solver-cost diagnostics, hard mass diagnostics and deterministic runtime/process publication within the frozen profiles.
Excluded optional physics does not become mandatory persistent state or worker cost. RB1 restart and runtime profiles preserve optionality and avoid solver scratch persistence.
Tile fractions, MODFLOW mappings and transfer-zone composition remain outside the SWAP kernel. RB1 makes no contrary composition assumption.
RB1 introduces no implicit midnight start, one-day duration, .swp parsing or direct-MODFLOW assumption. Unsupported configuration is required to fail closed.
F-RB01 explicitly audits every architecture invariant here and ties release readiness to zero applicable FAIL results.

nonclaim: PASS means the frozen RB1 subset preserves the SWAP5 architecture invariants. It does not qualify the excluded coupling, deep-vadose, RossFast or future-process capabilities themselves.
